content.value_statement: Logseq DB graphs can be difficult to query with raw Datalog. This skill provides reusable patterns for filters, pulls, rules, dates, and aggregations.
actual_capabilities: Builds Datalog query patterns for Logseq DB graphs.
Explains find, input, and where clauses in Datascript queries.
Shows pull syntax for attributes, tags, children, and reverse references.
Creates examples for tasks, journals, classes, properties, and date ranges.
Suggests query optimization practices, including selective clauses and limited pulls.
limitations: Does not execute queries or validate results against a live Logseq graph.
Requires users to provide graph schema details, property names, and expected output.
Examples target Logseq DB graphs and may need changes for markdown-based graphs.
Does not manage Logseq data or modify pages.

use_cases.title: Build Task Dashboards
use_cases.description: Create queries for task status, priority, deadlines, and overdue work in a Logseq DB graph.

use_cases.title: Create Plugin Queries
use_cases.description: Design Datascript queries for plugin features that read pages, blocks, tags, and properties.

use_cases.title: Analyze Knowledge Graph Metadata
use_cases.description: Find journals, classes, properties, and linked blocks for structured knowledge graph review.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Basic Query
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple Logseq DB query.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Logseq Datalog query for blocks tagged as Task. Return the title, status, and deadline fields.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Simple Query Syntax
prompt_templates.scenario: User has a Logseq query and wants full Datalog.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this Logseq simple query into full Datalog. Explain each clause and keep the result fields selective.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Slow Query
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Logseq Datalog query for performance. Suggest selective clauses, narrower pull fields, and safer result limits.

prompt_templates.title: Design Reusable Query Rules
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced user needs shared logic across queries.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design reusable Datalog rules for tagged tasks, overdue deadlines, and class inheritance. Include how each rule should be used.

output_examples.input: Find all open high priority tasks due before today.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines a Datalog query plan that filters task blocks by status, priority, and deadline, then pulls useful display fields.

output_examples.input: Show pages that extend a specific class and include their parent class names.
output_examples.output: The response explains which class and property attributes to match, how to bind parent names, and how to avoid broad pulls.

output_examples.input: Improve a query that pulls every attribute from thousands of blocks.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends selective fields, earlier filters, and smaller result shapes to reduce Logseq Datascript work.

best_practices: Provide exact Logseq class names, property names, and expected result fields.
Ask for selective pull fields when the graph is large.
Test generated queries on a small scope before using them in dashboards.
anti_patterns: Do not request broad wildcard pulls for large graphs.
Do not assume markdown graph attributes work unchanged in DB graphs.
Do not omit sample data when property names or status values are custom.

faq.question: Does this skill run Logseq queries?
faq.answer: No. It provides query patterns and explanations, but it does not execute queries against a graph.

faq.question: Can it help with Logseq DB graphs?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples focus on Logseq DB graph attributes, tags, classes, properties, and journals.

faq.question: Can it convert simple Logseq queries?
faq.answer: Yes. It can translate simple query intent into full Datalog structure for review and adaptation.

faq.question: Does it support plugin development?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Datascript query patterns that can inform Logseq plugin API usage.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide class names, property names, sample values, expected fields, and any performance constraints.

faq.question: Can it optimize slow queries?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest selective clauses, narrower pulls, and smaller result shapes for better performance.
